items.title: 78 nautical miles north of Fujairah, UAE, United Arab Emirates: Reuters reported that the UAE has secretly resumed limited crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, using tankers with tracking systems switched off; ADNOC shipped at least 6 million barrels in April aboard four tankers, with cargoes transferred offshore, stored in Oman, or sent to South Korea and Malaysia.
items.description: Reuters reported that the UAE has secretly resumed limited crude exports through the Strait of Hormuz, using tankers with tracking systems switched off; ADNOC shipped at least 6 million barrels in April aboard four tankers, with cargoes transferred offshore, stored in Oman, or sent to South Korea and Malaysia.
items.rawSummary: Amid ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations over the blockade, the Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, though the UAE has resumed covert oil exports and Iran has released footage of a seized container ship to underscore its control.
items.analysis: Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran have produced a 14-point draft memorandum to suspend enrichment and lift sanctions, though the Wall Street Journal indicated the Strait of Hormuz dispute is expected to remain unresolved. Subsequent reports suggested Iran and the U.S. have agreed to ease the naval blockade in exchange for Iran gradually reopening the strait, but Iranian President Pezeshkian has said any talks require the U.S. blockade to be lifted first. Iran’s state media now reports that all vessels must secure approval from its naval forces to transit and that no ships are currently passing; shipping intelligence sources confirm a new authority to manage transits and no vessel movement in recent days, while the U.S. escort operation, Project Freedom, was paused after Saudi Arabia denied access to its bases, with only two of roughly 1,600 stranded vessels guided through. In a development that challenges the official picture of a fully blocked waterway, Reuters revealed the UAE quietly moved at least 6 million barrels of crude in April aboard four tankers with their automatic identification systems switched off; maritime trade firms later added that such covert shipments occurred during both the U.S. and Iranian blockades and may understate previously reported export volumes. Iran released footage of the MSC Francesca, a container ship seized in the Strait of Hormuz earlier in the conflict, which further signals its assertion of control over the strait.

items.title: Islamabad, Pakistan: Pakistani sources said Iran could deliver its response to the U.S. through Pakistani mediators today.
items.description: Pakistani sources said Iran could deliver its response to the U.S. through Pakistani mediators today.
items.rawSummary: U.S.-Iran negotiations mediated by Pakistan are approaching a pivotal moment, with Iran expected to deliver its response to the latest U.S. proposal as Foreign Minister Araghchi travels to Islamabad and the two sides continue drafting a 14-point framework addressing enrichment, sanctions, and Strait of Hormuz transit.
items.analysis: The indirect talks, mediated by Pakistan, have entered a decisive phase, with Iranian President Pezeshkian meeting Supreme Leader Khamenei and Foreign Minister Araghchi departing for Islamabad, signaling Tehran's readiness to reply to Washington's formal counter-proposal imminently. The U.S. earlier responded to Iran's 14-point plan, focusing on enriched uranium as the central dispute, while the Wall Street Journal reported that both sides are drafting a 14-point framework to restart negotiations, possibly resuming in Islamabad next week and involving easing Iranian restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz and scaling back U.S. pressure on Iranian ports. Iran dropped its precondition of ending the U.S. blockade before ceasefire talks and is open to discussing its nuclear program in exchange for sanctions relief, though major disagreements persist over enrichment levels, sanctions, and control of the strait. President Trump told Congress that hostilities have terminated, arguing the ceasefire negates the War Powers Resolution deadline, even as U.S. troops remain in the region and the blockade continues, and he acknowledged Pakistan's opening of land routes with Iran. Confidence-building steps continue, including the recent evacuation of 22 crew from the Iranian vessel MV Touska, which is being moved to Pakistani waters for repairs.

items.title: Beijing, China, China: Bloomberg reported that China’s largest banks were instructed to temporarily freeze new loans to five refiners sanctioned by the U.S. over their ties to Iranian oil.
items.description: Bloomberg reported that China’s largest banks were instructed to temporarily freeze new loans to five refiners sanctioned by the U.S. over their ties to Iranian oil.
items.rawSummary: Amid Iran nuclear diplomacy and preparations for a Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, a Chinese military court sentences two former defense ministers to death with reprieves for corruption, while Bloomberg reports that China’s largest banks have been told to freeze loans to Iranian-oil-linked refiners under U.S. sanctions.
items.analysis: Beijing has been a focal point for Iran-related diplomacy in recent days, with Foreign Minister Wang Yi hosting his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi to discuss nuclear issues, regional security, and mutual opposition to U.S. sanctions. Unconfirmed reports suggest a preliminary 30-day U.S.-Iran peace deal is under discussion, involving uranium removal and asset-freeze easing, with Saudi mediation praised and Iran-Saudi talks encouraged by China. In parallel, Chinese state media confirmed that a military court sentenced former defense ministers Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu to death with a two-year reprieve for corruption; Reuters noted that neither will be eligible for parole or further commutation once the reprieves convert to life imprisonment. Adding a new layer of economic pressure, Bloomberg reported that China’s largest banks have been ordered to temporarily freeze new loans to five refiners sanctioned by the U.S. over their Iranian oil ties, underscoring the sanctions’ reach despite Beijing’s diplomatic backing for Tehran. Persistent allegations that Chinese firms supply drone components to Iran and Russia further complicate the picture as Beijing also prepares for a mid-May Trump summit, logistically signaled by four U.S. C-17 transport aircraft at its capital airport.

items.analysis: Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran have produced a 14-point draft memorandum to suspend enrichment and lift sanctions, though the Wall Street Journal indicated the Strait of Hormuz dispute is expected to remain unresolved. Iran’s state media now reports that all vessels must secure approval from its naval forces to transit and that no ships are currently passing; shipping intelligence sources confirm a new authority to manage transits and no vessel movement in recent days, while the U.S. escort operation, Project Freedom, was paused after Saudi Arabia denied access to its bases, with only two of roughly 1,600 stranded vessels guided through. items.title: Istanbul, Turkey: TUSAŞ CEO Mehmet Demiroğlu confirmed preliminary government-to-government talks with Spain over a potential KAAN sale, which would be the first export of a Turkish fifth-generation fighter to a NATO/EU country.
items.description: TUSAŞ CEO Mehmet Demiroğlu confirmed preliminary government-to-government talks with Spain over a potential KAAN sale, which would be the first export of a Turkish fifth-generation fighter to a NATO/EU country.
items.rawSummary: Turkey's SAHA 2026 defense exhibition in Istanbul featured the unveiling of advanced indigenous missile systems, the first KAAN stealth fighter serial production contract, and confirmation of preliminary talks with Spain over a potential KAAN export, underscoring Ankara's efforts to expand its domestic defense industry and international procurement partnerships.
items.analysis: At the SAHA 2026 exhibition in Istanbul, Turkey presented a full-scale mockup of the Eurofighter Typhoon, marking its first modern fighter acquisition from a non-U.S. supplier, and showcased the TAYFUN Block 4 hypersonic ballistic missile. ROKETSAN introduced the Neşter smart gliding munition, a precision kinetic weapon designed to minimize collateral damage, while the Ministry of Defense R&D center unveiled the Yıldırımhan intercontinental ballistic missile with a claimed range of 6,000 km and speeds between Mach 9 and 25. On the second day of the exhibition, Turkey signed its first serial production contract for the KAAN fifth-generation stealth fighter, moving the jet from development into domestic production, and the following day TUSAŞ's CEO confirmed preliminary government-to-government talks with Spain over a potential KAAN sale, which would be the first export of a Turkish stealth fighter to a NATO/EU member. The exhibition highlights Ankara's push to broaden military procurement sources and advance indigenous long-range strike and precision weapons programs.
